findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkbox items, not plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: Tasks 2C, 3C, 4C, 5C and 6C (lines 71, 94, 117, 126, 134) are written as `- [ ] **Task NC: Commit** — ...`. Commit markers must be plain `**Commit**: <message>` lines, never checkboxes. With a checkbox, each commit has to be followed by another edit to tick that box. That edit either goes into the next task's commit or becomes a commit that only ticks boxes, which project rules forbid ("Never make a commit that only checks boxes or only adds notes"). The markers are in the right places: after a tested unit for 2/2T, 3/3T and 4/4T, plus the conditional ones after 5 and 6. Only the format needs changing, for example `**Commit**: feat(core): add slice design heading validator`. The conditional wording for 5C and 6C can stay as plain text.

findings.title: Functional success criteria are all covered
findings.description:
- PASS on existing designs: Task 4T real-design run, Task 5 parity sweep.
- FAIL with `missing:` lines: Tasks 3T and 4T.
- doctype failure: Tasks 3T and 4T, including the quoted `docType` leniency.
- Multiple files in order with exit 1: Tasks 3T and 4T.
- Exit-2 cases with empty stdout in both modes, including valid-file-then-missing and the `cf guides update` message: Tasks 3T and 4T.
- `--json` contract: Task 4T.
- Template read from the worktree's own guide: Task 4T.

findings.title: Technical success criteria are all covered
findings.description:
- Normalization and matching unit tests (case, whitespace, comments, parentheticals, placeholder prefix, level mismatch, fenced headings, CRLF): Task 2T.
- Real-template test checking `## Overview` and `### Verification Walkthrough`: Task 3T.
- Real slice designs including 214: Task 4T.
- Build, lint, full suite and the ~300-line limit: Task 6.

The integration requirement (the guide repoints its references) is guide-side and correctly left as a post-release item in the Context Summary.

findings.title: Sequencing, test-with pattern and proportionality
findings.description:
- The order is: constant → pure validator → file layer (uses Task 2's functions) → CLI (uses Tasks 1 and 3) → walkthrough → docs. There are no circular dependencies.
- Each test task immediately follows its implementation task.
- There are three source files and three test files, matching the design's component list.
- Steps restate design decisions and do not add new ones.
- No NFR is stated, so no load test or CI gating is needed.

findings.title: Task 0 hard-codes `main` instead of using the resolved target
findings.description: The git rules make the branch fork from `{target}`, where target is `cf config get git.integration_branch` or `main` if that is empty. Task 0 hard-codes `main` and stops if the value is set. Wording it as `git checkout -b 214-slice.native-slice-design-validation {target}` follows the rule directly and removes the need to stop.

findings.title: Path handling between the CLI and core is not pinned down
findings.description: Task 3's result uses "`path` as given", and Task 4 prints "paths exactly as given". Neither task says whether the CLI passes raw arguments to core or paths resolved against the checkout or `--project`. If the CLI resolves them first, the printed paths would no longer match the contract. Task 4T's `FAIL <path>` assertions would catch this, but one line in Task 4 would prevent it: "pass the arguments to core unchanged; resolve only the template path."

findings.title: Template with no required headings is only tested in core, not through the CLI
findings.description: Task 3T checks that a template with no markers throws `SliceDesignValidationError`. Task 4T checks exit 2 with empty stdout only for the missing-template case. Both go through the same `handleError(err, 2)` path, so the risk is low. Adding a no-markers template fixture to the Task 4T exit-2 list would cover this success criterion end to end at small cost.

findings.title: It is unclear whether the "original heading text" includes the `#` markers
findings.description: Task 2 says `RequiredHeading` keeps "original heading text for messages", but not whether that is the full trimmed line (`## Value`) or just the text (`Value`). The output contract (`missing: ## Value`) and the assertions in Tasks 3T and 4T need the full line. Stating that in Task 2 avoids having to rework it after the tests fail.
